questions.q: Why write the readable, names-joined version of the query before the keys-only staged version?
options: There is no reason, both versions are identical
Because SQL Server requires names before keys can be used
Because keys-only queries run slower
So you can eyeball and sanity-check the data before committing to the staged shape
questions.explain: Writing the readable version first lets you verify the data makes sense before Lesson 4 strips it down to keys only.

questions.q: Why is Product joined to ProductSubcategory with a LEFT JOIN instead of an INNER JOIN?
options: ProductSubcategory doesn't support INNER JOIN
It makes the query run in alphabetical order
LEFT JOIN is required whenever more than three tables are joined
Some products have a NULL ProductSubcategoryID, and an inner join would silently drop those order lines
questions.explain: A handful of AdventureWorks2012 products have no subcategory assigned; LEFT JOIN keeps those rows instead of dropping them.

questions.q: What does WHERE soh.Status = 5 filter the query to?
options: Shipped orders only
Orders from exactly 5 territories
Orders placed exactly 5 days ago
Orders with exactly 5 line items
questions.explain: Status 5 is AdventureWorks2012's code for a Shipped order — the scope both stakeholders' numbers should reflect.

questions.q: Why does the query pull DueDate and ShipDate even though no report page uses them yet?
options: The Operations Manager's fulfillment metric and Lesson 15's change request will both need them
To make the query run faster
They are unrelated columns included by accident
They are required columns in every SELECT statement
questions.explain: Pulling fulfillment columns now, while already in this query, is cheaper than adding them to a view later.

questions.q: What should you check after running this lesson's query against AdventureWorks2012?
options: That it includes every table in the database
That it returns exactly 100 rows
That its row count matches the COUNT(*) from Lesson 2's grain-check query
That it runs in under one second
questions.explain: Matching row counts confirms no join is dropping or duplicating order-line rows before this becomes a view in Lesson 4.
